translations.text: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert, and so on.
I would like to expound to you this gospel that was just read before you, but I fear that you cannot understand the great depth of the gospel as fully as would be fitting.
Now I ask you to be patient in your minds until, with God's help, we can read through the exposition.
"Jesus was led by the Holy Spirit into a wilderness, so that he might be tempted by the devil.
And then he fasted forty days and forty nights, so that he tasted neither food nor drink in all that time; but afterwards he was hungry.
Then the tempter approached and said to him, 'If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to be turned into bread.'
Then Jesus answered and said, 'It is written: man does not live by bread alone, but lives by all the words that come out of God's mouth.'
Then the devil took him and set him on the pinnacle of the high temple, and said, 'If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down now;
it is written that the angels are commanded concerning you, that they will lift you up in their hands, so that you need not even strike your foot against a stone.'
Then Jesus said to him again, 'It is written: Do not tempt your Lord.'
Then the devil took him again and set him on a very high mountain, and showed him the wealth of the whole world and its glory, and said to him,
'All these things I will give you, if you will fall at my feet and worship me.' Then Jesus said to him, 'Get behind me, Satan!'"
"It is written, Everyone shall worship his Lord alone and serve him alone. Then the devil left him, and angels came to him and ministered to him."
The Holy Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness so that he might be tempted there.
Now everyone wonders how the devil dared approach Jesus to tempt him; but he would not have dared to tempt Christ if he had not been permitted.
Jesus came to mankind because he wished to overcome all our temptations by his temptations, and to overcome our eternal death by his temporary death.
Now he was so humble that he allowed the devil to tempt him, and he allowed wicked men to kill him.
The devil is the head of all unrighteous men, and evil men are his limbs; now God allowed the head to tempt him, and the limbs to hang him.
The devil was in great doubt: what was Christ? His life was not ordered like other men's lives.
Christ did not eat greedily, nor did he drink to excess, nor did his eyes wander roaming after various desires.
Then the devil considered what he was; whether he was the Son of God who had been promised to mankind. He then said in his mind that he would test what he was.
When Christ fasted forty days and forty nights without a break, the devil did not tell him to eat at any time in that whole period, because he saw that he was not hungry at all.
Again, when Christ was hungry after so long a time, the devil truly supposed that he was not God, and said to him,
"Why are you hungry? If you are the Son of God, turn these stones into loaves, and eat."
God could easily have done it, he who turned water into wine and who made all creatures out of nothing; he could easily have turned the stones into bread;
but he would do nothing at the devil's direction; instead he said to him in answer, "Man does not live by bread alone, but lives by the words that come out of God's mouth."
Just as a man's body lives by bread, so must his soul live by God's words, that is, by God's teaching, which he has set down in books through wise men.
If the body has no food, or cannot take food, then it wastes away and dies;
so too the soul, if it lacks holy teaching, will waste away and be without strength. Through holy teaching it is strong and stirred to God's will.

So the devil was overcome by Christ for the first time. "And he then took him and carried him up onto the temple, and set him on the pinnacle, and said to him, If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down;
for the angels have been commanded concerning you that they shall lift you up in their hands, so that you need not strike your foot against a stone."
Here the devil began to expound the holy scriptures, and he lied in his account, because he is false, and there is no truth in him; rather, he is the father of every lie.
What he then said was not written about Christ, but was written about holy people: they need the help of angels in this life, so that the devil may not tempt them as severely as he would like.
God is so gracious to mankind that he has set his angels as guardians over us, so that they must never allow the cruel devils to be able to destroy us.
They are allowed to tempt us, but they are not allowed to force us into any evil, unless we do it ourselves of our own will, through the evil prompting of the devil.
We are not made perfect unless we are tested: through testing we must thrive, if we always renounce the devil and all his teachings;
and if we draw near to our Lord with faith, and love, and good works; and if we slip anywhere, we must rise again at once and eagerly repair what has been broken there.
Christ then said to the devil, "One must not tempt one's Lord."
It would have been a very boastful deed if Christ had thrown himself down then, though he could easily have leapt down without injury to his limbs, he who bent the high arch of heaven;
but he would do nothing out of boastfulness, because boastfulness is a capital sin. So he would not throw himself down, because he shunned boastfulness; but he said, "One must not tempt one's Lord."
That person tempts his Lord who, with foolish confidence and with boastfulness, wants to do some wondrous thing in God's name, or who wants to ask God for some miracle foolishly and without need.
Then the devil was overcome a second time through Christ's patience.

"Then he took him again and carried him up onto a mountain, and showed him the wealth of the whole world and its glory, and said to him, All these things I will give you, if you will fall down at my feet and worship me."
The devil spoke presumptuously here, just as he had spoken before, when he was in heaven, when he wanted to share the kingdom of heaven with his Creator and be like God;
but his presumption cast him down into hell then; and now too his presumption brought him low, when, through Christ's passion, he lost mankind from his power.
He said, "These things I will give you." It seemed to him that he owned the whole world, because no one had withstood him before Christ came, who subdued him.
It is written in the holy books, "The earth and all its fullness, and the whole world and those who dwell in it, all of it is God's possession," and not the devil's.
Nevertheless, Christ said in his gospel concerning the devil that he was the prince of the world, and that he would be cast out.
He is the prince of those people who love this world and set all their hope on this life, and despise their Creator.
All creatures, the sun and moon and all the stars, land and sea and beasts, all of them serve their Creator, because they move according to God's ordinance.
The wicked person alone, when he despises God's commandments and carries out the devil's will, whether through avarice, or through lying,
or through anger, or through other sins, then becomes the devil's servant, since he pleases the devil and despises the one who made him.
"Christ then said to the devil, Get back, Satan! It is written, One shall worship his Lord and serve him alone."
Some say that the Saviour did not say, "Satan, get behind," but only "Go"; but in the more correct and older copies we have,
"Get behind, Satan," as the interpretation of the name itself shows; for "devil" is interpreted as "rushing downward." So to the apostle Peter Christ says,
"Get behind me," that is, Follow me. To the devil it is not said, "Get behind me," but "Get behind," as we have already said, and so the blessed Jerome wrote in one of his letters.
He said to the devil, "Go behind." The devil's name is interpreted as "Falling-down."
He fell down, and went backward, from the very beginning of his existence, when he was cut off from the heavenly bliss; he went backward again through Christ's coming;
he shall go backward on Doomsday, when he will be locked in hell-torment, in eternal fire, he and all his companions; and they will never afterward be able to break out.
It is written in the old law that no one shall pray to any idol, or to any thing, except to God alone;
because no created thing is worthy of that honour except him alone who is the Creator of all things: to him alone we must pray; he alone is true Lord and true God.
We ask holy people for intercession, that they should intercede for us with their Lord and our Lord;
Nevertheless, we do not pray to them as we do to God, nor will they allow it; as the angel said to John the apostle when he was about to fall at his feet. He said,
"Do not do it; do not bow down to me. I am God's servant, as you and your brothers are: pray to God alone."
"Then the devil left Christ, and angels came to him and ministered to him." He was tempted as a man, and after the temptation holy angels came to him and ministered to him as to their Creator.
Unless the devil had seen that Christ was a man, he would not have tempted him; and unless he were true God, the angels would not have been willing to minister to him.
Great was our Saviour's humility and his patience in this deed,
He could have sunk the devil into the deep abyss with a single word; but he did not show his might. Instead he answered the devil with holy scripture,
and he gave us an example by his patience, that as often as we suffer anything from perverse people, we should turn our minds to God's teaching rather than to any revenge.
The devil's temptation comes in three ways: that is, by suggestion, by delight, and by consent. The devil incites us to evil, but we must shun it and take no delight in the suggestion.
but if our mind takes pleasure in it, then we must at least resist, so that there is no consent to the evil deed.
The evil suggestion comes from the devil; then a person's mind is often bent toward delight, and sometimes also slips into consent, because we are born of sinful flesh.
The Saviour was not tempted in that way, because he was born of a virgin without sin, and there was nothing perverse in him.
He could be tempted by suggestion, but no delight touched his mind.
Nor was there any consent there, because there was no delight there; and so the devil's temptation was entirely outside him, and nothing within.
The devil came to Christ uncertain, and went away uncertain, because the Saviour did not reveal his power to him, but patiently drove him off with the holy scriptures.
The old devil tempted our father Adam in three ways: that is, with gluttony, with vainglory, and with covetousness;
and then he was overcome, because he consented to the devil in all three temptations.
He was overcome through gluttony when, at the devil's urging, he ate the forbidden apple.
He was overcome through vainglory when he believed the devil's words, when he said, "You will be as great as the angels, if you eat of the tree."
And they believed his lie, and in vain boasting wished to be better than they had been created; then they became worse.
He was overcome by covetousness when the devil said to him, "And you will have knowledge of both good and evil."
Covetousness is not in money alone, but is also in the desire for great dignity.
With the same three things by which the devil overcame the first-created man, with those same things Christ overcame him and laid him low. The devil tempted Christ through gluttony when he said,
"Tell these stones to be turned into loaves, and eat." He tempted him through vainglory when he urged him to throw himself down from the pinnacle of the temple.
Through covetousness he tempted him when he falsely promised him the wealth of the whole world, if he would fall at his feet.

But the devil was then overcome by Christ in the same ways by which he had earlier overcome Adam, so that he might depart from our hearts, made captive by the same way of entry by which he had entered in and made us captive.
We have heard in this gospel that our Lord fasted forty days and forty nights continuously. When he fasted so long,
he then revealed the great might of his divinity, through which he could have lived through all this present life without earthly food, if he had wished.
Again, when he was hungry, he revealed that he was a true man and therefore needed food.
Moses the leader also fasted forty days and forty nights, so that he might receive God's law; but he did not fast through his own power, but through God's.
The prophet Elijah also fasted just as long, likewise through God's power, and afterwards was taken from this life without death.
Now this fast is appointed for all Christian people to keep in the course of every year; but we may each day partake of our food with abstinence, of those foods that are permitted.
Why is this fast thus reckoned at forty days? In the whole year there are reckoned three hundred and sixty-five days;
then, if we tithe these days of the year, there will be thirty-six tithe-days; and from this day until the holy Easter Day there are forty-two days:
take then the six Sundays out of that number, and then the thirty-six tithe-days of the year are reckoned for us for abstinence.

Just as God's law commands us that we must give God the tithe of all the things that come to us from our year's labour, so we must also on these tithe-days tithe our body with abstinence to the praise of God.
We must prepare ourselves in all things as God's servants, according to the apostle's teaching, in great patience, and in holy vigils, in fasts, and in purity of mind and body;
Therefore it is less dangerous for a Christian to eat meat than to have relations with a woman in this holy season.
Put away all quarrels and every dispute, and keep this season with peace and with true love; for no fast is acceptable to God without peace.
And do as God taught: break your bread and give the other part to a hungry man, and bring into your house the needy and the poor strangers, and comfort them with your goods.
When you see a naked man, clothe him, and do not despise your own flesh.
The man who fasts without giving alms acts as if he were only saving his food, and afterwards he eats what he had earlier gone without through abstinence; but God condemns that fast.
But if you want to fast to please God, then help poor people with the portion that you deny yourself, and with more as well if you can afford it.
Avoid idle talk and foolish merriment, and weep for your sins; for Christ said, "Woe to you who laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep."
Again he said, "Blessed are those who weep now, for they shall be comforted."
We live in various ways over the twelve months. Now, in this season, we must make up for our negligence and live for God, we who at other times lived for ourselves.
And whatever good we do, let us do it without boasting or idle praise.
The man who does any good deed out of vainglory, to win praise for himself, has no reward for it from God, but has his punishment instead.
But let us do as God taught, so that our good works are known to people in such a way that they can see our goodness, and that they may glorify and praise our Heavenly Father,
[?] God Almighty, who repays a hundredfold whatever we do for poor people out of love for him, who lives and reigns for ever without end, in eternity. Amen.
